items.followUp: Why is the value of g greater at the poles than at the equator?

rubric.why: Earth’s shape means its radius and distance from its centre vary from place to place.
rubric.description: Connects the variation in g to Earth’s shape or varying radius.
rubric.how: Award for stating that Earth is not a perfect sphere or that its radius differs from place to place.

rubric.why: The model answer gives the resulting pole-equator comparison and notes other ways g varies.
rubric.description: Gives a correct comparison or another location-dependent variation in g.
rubric.how: Award for a correct comparison between the equator and poles, or for stating that g changes with altitude or depth.

modelAnswer: The value of g varies from place to place because the Earth is not a perfect sphere; its radius is greater at the equator than at the poles.
Therefore, g is smaller at the equator and greater at the poles; it also changes with altitude and depth.

items.followUp: Define Young’s modulus and write its formula in terms of force, area, length and extension.

accept: ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain
tensile stress divided by tensile strain
rubric.why: Young’s modulus is defined as the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain.

rubric.why: The mathematical form expresses the definition directly or expands stress and strain in terms of force and dimensions.
rubric.description: Writes the mathematical form of Young’s modulus.
rubric.how: Award for the stress-to-strain formula or an equivalent expanded formula.

modelAnswer: Young’s modulus is the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain within the elastic limit.

items.followUp: A vehicle has a weight of 15 kN and a speed of 12 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy. Take g = 10 m/s².

rubric.why: The weight is recorded in SI units for calculating the mass.
rubric.description: Records or converts the car’s weight correctly.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the car weighs 12 kN or 12000 N.

rubric.why: Mass is found from weight using W = mg; with g = 10 m/s², the mass is 1200 kg.
rubric.description: Finds the car’s mass from its weight.
rubric.how: Award for using m = W/g or obtaining 1200 kg.

rubric.why: The kinetic energy formula is required to calculate the car’s energy.
Substituting the mass and speed into the formula gives the kinetic energy.
rubric.description: Substitutes the mass and speed correctly.
rubric.how: Award for a correct substitution using 1200 kg and 20 m/s.

rubric.why: The calculation gives a kinetic energy of 240000 J, equivalent to 240 kJ.
rubric.description: Gives the kinetic energy with a correct unit.
rubric.how: Award for 240000 J or its equivalent, 240 kJ.

modelAnswer: Given: W = 12 kN = 12000 N, v = 20 m/s, g = 10 m/s².
The kinetic energy of the car is 240000 J, or 240 kJ.
